title: The Spire of Highmoor
premise: Mara Vasquez flees her hedge-witch master into the Thornfell mountains only to discover the old gods are waking — and the first to answer a prayer is Veyra, the goddess of oaths, who names Mara her reluctant vessel. Hunted by the Spire of Highmoor's inquisitors, who have kept the gods sealed for three centuries, Mara joins a ragged band of smugglers and a disgraced Spire knight who becomes her found family — and her forbidden love. As Veyra's power grows inside her, Mara learns the 'ancient war' the Spire fears reigniting was actually a divine massacre the Spire itself committed to seize the gods' magic. In the end, Mara shatters the Spire's seal rather than let them kill the waking gods, sacrificing Veyra's gift and nearly her own life, and chooses her chosen family over the duty both sides tried to force upon her.
about_author: Emrys Villalobos is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent five years leading treks through remote mountain passes and now writes fantasy from a cabin at the edge of a national forest. Their work is known for morally tangled magic, weather-beaten landscapes, and found families forged under impossible odds.

chapters.title: The Debt of Salt and Smoke
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Fleeing her master's debts through the Thornfell smuggler roads, Mara shelters in a ruined shrine and, out of desperation, prays aloud for the first time in years. Something answers. The chapter ends with a voice like struck bronze naming her, and the emotional beat is the terror of being truly seen after a lifetime of hiding.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Answered
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The goddess Veyra, goddess of oaths, manifests through Mara's reflection, bound to her by an accidental vow. Mara tries to outrun her own god and stumbles into a Spire patrol; she is saved by Kaelen, a disgraced knight who recognizes divine fire when he sees it. Beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: The Spire's Long Silence
chapters.summary: Kaelen's POV. Kaelen reveals the Spire of Highmoor has executed god-speakers for three hundred years, and he was cast out for questioning one such killing. The smugglers of Thornfell's Hollow — gruff Ferro, sharp-tongued twins Isolde and Bram — hide the pair. Beat: the fragile first stitches of found family, laced with Kaelen's guilt.

chapters.title: Prayers in the Dark
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Other prayers are being answered across the mountains — small miracles, desperate voices. Mara realizes Veyra is only the first god waking, and the Spire is burning shrines to stop the rest. She chooses to carry warning to the hollow shrines. Beat: the shift from fugitive to reluctant herald.

chapters.title: Ash on the Pilgrim's Road
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The smugglers escort Mara to a mountain shrine; they arrive after the Spire's inquisitors have burned it and its keeper. Isolde, who lost family to the Spire's purges, confronts her rage while Mara channels Veyra to save a dying child. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose; the crew stops being hired hands and becomes kin.

chapters.title: The Oath Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Kaelen's POV. Veyra leads them to a glacier vault where the gods were sealed — and Kaelen finds records proving the Spire's founders murdered the gods to steal their power, then wrote the 'ancient war' as cover. Mara and Kaelen, exhausted and raw, admit their feelings. Beat: love declared against the duty that forbids it.

chapters.title: A Crown of Quiet Lies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Veyra's power begins consuming Mara's memories, offering to erase her pain — and her attachments — to make her a perfect vessel. Mara glimpses how the Spire's High Inquisitor was once a god-speaker hollowed the same way. Beat: the seduction of power, and Mara's first refusal of it at real cost.

chapters.title: The March on Highmoor
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Spire captures Ferro and the twins' brother to bait a trap; the crew mounts a desperate rescue that becomes a full assault on Highmoor's lower city as waking gods stir the populace. Bram's humor cracks to reveal fear of losing the family he never expected. Beat: the point of no return, paid for in blood.

chapters.title: Where Gods Go to Die
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Climax. In the Spire's seal-chamber, the High Inquisitor offers Mara Veyra's throne: become the last god, orderly and alone, and end the chaos. Veyra herself begs Mara to break the seal even if it unmakes them both. Mara shatters it, freeing the gods and burning out Veyra's gift in her own veins. Beat: love and freedom chosen over power and safety.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down the Mountain
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Resolution. The gods walk the world again on their own terms; the Spire fractures into reform and exile. Magicless, half-deaf from the seal's breaking, Mara descends Thornfell with Kaelen and the crew — not apprentices, not vessels, not knights, just family. Beat: quiet, earned peace and an open horizon.
